h13.rule: auth on, 20 rovers: the busiest link's load (p95 over draws) <= 16 kbit/s at 1 Hz position reports, and > 16 kbit/s at 10 Hz

driving_split.note: python tools/atc/run_b103.py        # -> results/E53_bitrate.json key "driving_split", rows added to E53_table.csv

e40_month.note: default link rule (mesh line of sight within 5 km), as E48 month_links 'default'; driving = the robot's route sample one minute after the epoch differs

status_intent_at_1hz.note: POSITION, STATUS and INTENT each at 1 Hz, authenticated; HELLO then not sent (it only fills up to 1 Hz); event messages as E53

lrip_v02.task: B-100 (P3 M4, P1 M10; decisions B3)
changes_from_v0.1: POSITION: the 6 spare bits carry u95_code, a 95 % horizontal position bound on a log scale (no byte added)
HELLO: appends frame_id (6 bits), datum_id (6 bits) and time_scale (4 bits): the sender's declaration of the frame, datum and time scale of every position and time stamp it sends (2 bytes added)
HELLO is sent at least once every 10 s (declaration_interval_s), not only when nothing else was sent
enums frame, datum, time_scale added; manifest registry keys frame, datum, time_scale appended

declaration rule: a receiver accepts a POSITION only from a sender that has declared frame, datum and time scale in an authenticated HELLO or a signed manifest under the same key epoch (lunarsim/atc/lrip/codec.py Receiver)

framing_row.note: every packet in a Proximity-1 frame (+12 B); the published sizes are packets before link framing and coding

traffic_model_coverage.note: 11 of the 15 message types; announcements, capability queries / manifests and map notices are rare and not in the per-robot traffic model
